summary: Adds financial segments and invoiced amounts to the Phase 1 Layercake membership solution (schema Layercake), and changes how Retired members are recognised. Every membership event (Join, Change, Lapse, Readmission, Renewal) and paid member can be filtered by payment method, payer type (Individual or Corporate) and concession type. Segment values are held once per contact per Campaign Year in a new silv_member_year_attributes table and copied onto every event, with flags showing values carried forward from an earlier year. Every segment uses the same reserved values: Unknown (0), Unrecognised (-1) and Not applicable (-2). Each contact-year's invoiced amount in GBP comes from Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses ('Inv Total Amount'), landed in the Phase 1 brnz_subs_status. It is carried on one Join, Renewal or Readmission event as invoiced_subtotal_gbp (with subs_amount_gbp equal to it), with a status that explains any missing amount. The invoices set the segments and feed the anomaly checks, but never the revenue. Invoice lines are landed at the source's ledger-distribution grain, one row per (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue), and every reader takes a transaction's settled amount once per transaction. Corporate subscriptions are landed one row per contact, scheme and Campaign Year: where the source repeats a key, a fixed order picks the copy to keep, and the load no longer fails on it. A corporate subscription row with no Campaign Year is skipped and counted rather than landed, and does not stop the load. A retirement date derived from the first invoice with a retired concession replaces apuk_retirementdate in the Practising / Retired logic, so Phase 1 results split by membership status change. The employer segment is delivered as findings only. The daily load keeps every past daily count in line with the current silver data on every run, from 2020-10-01, with no manual step. It records each change to a past or repeated day in an adjustment history that gives the figures as known at any time. One call of Layercake.usp_run_daily_load also runs the payment and invoice segment loads. On a normal day the daily count recomputes only the contacts whose inputs changed, and the gold daily fact is synced cell by cell, with results identical to a full recompute. The daily member counts (silv_daily_count_detail and fact_daily_member_count_detail) are also split by payment method, payer type and concession type, taken from each contact's attributes for the Campaign Year of the day, with every total at the old grain unchanged. A member's local group (CE.vwContact.rics_localgroupid, through CE.vwLocalGroup) is a new reported dimension. On every date, the existing country and region fields carry the values that follow from the member's local group, so regional figures agree with the business's local-group-based figures and Power BI needs no change. The member's own country and its region are kept in new columns. Results split by region or country change, history included. All other Phase 1 counts and measures stay the same. This version applies amendments AMD-001 (Mike, 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-09), AMD-002 (invoice line grain, Mike, 2026-11-11), AMD-003 (daily load accuracy, Mike, 2026-11-17), AMD-004 (corporate subscription repeated keys, Mike, 2026-11-18), AMD-005 (corporate subscription rows with no Campaign Year, Mike, 2026-11-18), AMD-006 (daily load speed, Mike, 2026-11-19), AMD-007 (daily count payment segments, Mike, 2026-11-20) and AMD-008 (member region by local group, Mike, 2026-11-26) to the spec that made the twelve changes in Damian Watson's review of 20 October 2026. Items that need Finance or real-data profiling stay as open questions, each with a stated working default.

glossary.Campaign Year: The RICS subscription year, as held in Layercake.ref_campaign_year_config and on the invoice source (Subs.tblSubsInvoices.Campaign_Year).
glossary.Eligible invoice: A subscription invoice that may set a contact-year's segments and be matched to an event for the invoice checks (RULE-014, RULE-084). Credit notes and enrolment- or application-fee-only invoices are never eligible. A fully credited invoice is eligible only when the contact-year has no other eligible invoice.
glossary.Segment invoice: The eligible invoice that sets a contact-year's payment method, payer type and concession (RULE-079).
glossary.Amount Campaign Year: The Campaign Year whose member status row (Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses, landed in Layercake.brnz_subs_status) gives an event's amount, and in which the event is matched to an invoice for the checks: the event's own year for Renewal and Readmission, and the first paid position's year for a Join (RULE-032).
glossary.Live corporate subscription: A row in Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions for the contact and Campaign Year where both 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' are active (RULE-082).
glossary.Carried forward: A segment value copied from the latest earlier Campaign Year with an eligible invoice, because the year itself has none. Flagged by the *_carried columns.
glossary.Reserved values: Fixed ids in every segment reference table: 0 Unknown (the source has no value), -1 Unrecognised (the source has a value the mapping does not know), -2 Not applicable (no value is expected).
glossary.Headline value: invoiced_subtotal_gbp: the contact-year's invoiced amount in GBP (Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses 'Inv Total Amount'), carried on one event per contact and amount Campaign Year (RULE-033, RULE-098).
glossary.Invoice source coverage: Campaign Year 2022 onward. Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices keeps only Campaign_Year >= 2022.
glossary.Derived retirement date: The 'Renewal Date' of a contact's earliest Campaign Year that has a retired concession and a payment or settlement date (RULE-099). It drives Practising / Retired in place of apuk_retirementdate.
glossary.Invoice line: One row of Layercake.brnz_subs_invoice_line: one ledger distribution of an F&O customer transaction in synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS, identified by (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue). One customer transaction (one recid) can have many lines, for example one per cost centre or Campaign Year (RULE-104).
glossary.Daily count cell: One row of Layercake.silv_daily_count_detail: a [date] with its region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id, local_group_id and contact_country_id (REQ-026, REQ-027).
glossary.Seven daily measures: active_count, paid_count, paid_count_event, event_join_count, event_renewal_count, event_readmission_count and event_lapse_count on silv_daily_count_detail and silv_daily_count.
glossary.Adjustment: A change to a daily count cell's figures on a date that was already loaded, recorded once per run that made it as new minus old for each of the seven daily measures (REQ-019). The first load of a date is not an adjustment.
glossary.As known at: The figure for a date as it stood at a time T: today's stored figure minus the adjustments written after T (REQ-020).
glossary.Repeated corporate subscription key: A (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year) that appears on more than one row of Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions, because the view is at subscription-user grain. Bronze keeps one copy (RULE-128).
glossary.Corporate subscription row with no Campa: A row of Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions whose 'Sub Campaign Year' is NULL, because the subscription's licence key in CRM (CE.vwRicsv2Subscription.apuk_licensekey) is not yet set. It is skipped and counted, not landed (RULE-134, RULE-135).
glossary.Local group: The RICS local group a member belongs to: CE.vwContact.rics_localgroupid, described by CE.vwLocalGroup. From AMD-008 it sets the country and region the member is reported under, but only when it is usable: CE.vwLocalGroup holds it, it is active (statecode 0), it has a country, and it gives a region in both apuk_worldregionid_name and Market_reporting_region. Any other member keeps their own country and its region in every field, with local_group_id 0 Unknown (REQ-027, RULE-171, AMD-009).
glossary.Own country: The member's own country (CE.vwContact.rics_countryid), which set country_id and region before AMD-008. It is kept as contact_country_id, together with the region that country gives (REQ-027).

requirements.title: Phase 1 counts and measures unchanged
requirements.description: The new segments and amounts must not change any existing Phase 1 count. That covers active members, both paid measures, and Join, Renewal, Readmission and Lapse event counts by date and grade. Adding keys, flags and amounts to events must not change the number of events or their identifiers. Only two kinds of result change. Results split by membership status (Practising / Retired) change, because the derived retirement date (REQ-017) replaces apuk_retirementdate (Q-046). Results split by region or country change, history included, because region and country follow the member's local group (REQ-027). That overrides BR-001's rule that Phase 1 counts by region must not change (Mike, AMD-008, 2026-11-26). The Phase 1 difference scripts are re-baselined where region is involved, and must then read PASS. In this release acceptance runs on synthetic data only, and no pass threshold is set for real data (assumes Q-026).

requirements.title: Bronze landing of subscription invoices, invoice lines and member statuses
requirements.description: Land the subscription invoice data that Stories 1 to 4 need, from sources already in the warehouse. Invoice-level data (payment method, currency, credits, payment status, concession flags) comes from external table Subs.tblSubsInvoices into new Layercake.brnz_subs_invoice. Line-level data (item code, line amounts, payment lines and credits) comes from external table synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS into new Layercake.brnz_subs_invoice_line. Profiling of real data (Q-021, 2026-11-11) shows CUSTTRANS_RICS is at ledger-distribution grain: each customer transaction (RECID) is split into one row per POSTINGTYPE and ACCOUNTDISPLAYVALUE, the ledger account string that carries main account, cost centre, country, item code and, where set, Campaign Year. brnz_subs_invoice_line lands every row in scope at that grain, not aggregated, with the ledger columns that tell a transaction's lines apart (RULE-104). Every reader takes its transaction-level columns once per transaction (RULE-105). The Phase 1 Layercake.brnz_subs_status, which lands Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses on ([Contact No.], [Campaign Year]), gains 'Inv Total Amount' and 'Retired Concession', which the event amount (REQ-008) and the derived retirement date (REQ-017) need. Its existing 'Member Invoice Position' and 'Renewal Date' columns are used as they are. No second bronze table is created (Q-043).

business_rules.rule: Bronze tables are 1:1 copies of the source columns they land, with no transformation of values, plus the audit columns every existing bronze table carries (_loaded_at, _updated_at, _is_deleted, _deleted_at).

Each bronze load runs a row-count check: rows with _is_deleted = 0 equal the source rows in scope. For brnz_corporate_subscription the check compares the number of distinct (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year) keys among the source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year with the live rows (RULE-130, RULE-134). The load records its row counts through Layercake.usp_etl_log_start and Layercake.usp_etl_log_end.

Rows of synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS are in scope for brnz_subs_invoice_line when their ACCOUNTNUM and VOUCHER match an invoice in Subs.tblSubsInvoices (its lines of every RICINVOICETYPE), or their LASTSETTLEVOUCHER matches such a voucher (credits and payments settling it). This mirrors how Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices relates non-subscription lines and credits to an invoice.

Layercake.brnz_subs_status gains the source columns 'Inv Total Amount' and 'Retired Concession' of Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses, landed 1:1 like its existing columns, with no transformation. Its key ([Contact No.], [Campaign Year]), its existing columns and its rows are unchanged. No second bronze table lands Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses (Q-043).

Layercake.brnz_subs_invoice_line holds one row per synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS row in scope (RULE-077), identified by (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue). Rows are landed as they are and never aggregated. recid alone is not unique: it is the customer transaction's key, and one transaction is split into one row per POSTINGTYPE and ACCOUNTDISPLAYVALUE (Q-021). The design decides how the key is enforced.

amountcur and amountmst are the line's own amounts. settleamountcur, and CustTrans_AmountCur and CustTrans_AmountMst if they are used, are transaction-level values that repeat on every line of the same recid. Every reader of brnz_subs_invoice_line takes them once per recid and never sums them across a transaction's lines. Any count of transactions or invoices taken from brnz_subs_invoice_line counts distinct recid values, not rows (Q-021).

requirements.title: Member-year attributes with payment method
requirements.description: Create Layercake.silv_member_year_attributes, built before silv_membership_events. It holds one row per contact per Campaign Year, from the contact's first membership event to the current Campaign Year. This requirement defines which invoices are eligible: credit notes are excluded, and the case where every invoice is fully credited is defined (review change 5). It also defines which eligible invoice sets a contact-year's segments, and adds payment_method_id and payment_method_carried. REQ-006 and REQ-011 add payer type and concession on the same rules, so all segments use the same invoices (review change 8).

business_rules.rule: The table holds exactly one row per contact per Campaign Year, from the Campaign Year of the contact's first membership event to the current Campaign Year inclusive.

An invoice in Layercake.brnz_subs_invoice for the contact (account_num = contact_no) and Campaign Year is eligible when: (a) it is not a credit note, meaning its invoice number does not contain 'FTCN' and does not contain 'CRE' with a non-zero full_invoice_amount_cur (the owner's own test in Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices); (b) it is not fully credited (fully_credited is not 'Y'); and (c) its mapped lines are not all enrolment or application fee lines. Where a contact-year has no invoice meeting (a) to (c), its fully credited invoices that meet (a) and (c) are eligible instead (assumes Q-012). A credit note is never eligible.

Where a contact-year has more than one eligible invoice, the latest by trans_date is the segment invoice and sets the year's payment method, payer type and concession (assumes Q-012). Each event's amounts still come from its own invoice (RULE-032).
A contact-year's payment method is the payment mode of its segment invoice (brnz_subs_invoice.inv_payment_method), mapped through silv_ref_payment_method (assumes Q-001).

Where the segment invoice has no payment mode but its payment lines do, the method is the one covering the largest settled amount. A payment transaction's settled amount (settleamountcur) is counted once per recid, however many lines the transaction is split into, and is never summed across its lines (RULE-105). On a tie, the method of the earliest payment wins.
A Campaign Year that has an eligible invoice but no payment mode on the segment invoice or its payment lines gets Unknown (0) with payment_method_carried = 0.

A Campaign Year from 2022 onward with no eligible invoice takes the payment method of the latest earlier Campaign Year that has one, with payment_method_carried = 1. If no earlier year has one, it gets Unknown (0) with payment_method_carried = 0 (assumes Q-006).
Contact-years before 2022, the first Campaign Year the invoice source holds, get Not applicable (-2) for payment method, payer type and concession type, with every carried flag 0 (assumes Q-011).

No event amount is taken from brnz_subs_invoice or brnz_subs_invoice_line (Q-038, Q-042).

subs_amount_gbp = invoiced_subtotal_gbp on every Join, Renewal and Readmission event. The two are null together (Q-044).

requirements.title: Anomalies linking invoices and events
requirements.description: Record in Layercake.silv_data_anomaly the events with no matching invoice, the invoices with no event, data that breaks the one-invoice-per-event assumption, and Readmission events with no readmission fee. Each of these situations gets its own reason code (anomaly type). These checks match events to the invoices (brnz_subs_invoice and brnz_subs_invoice_line) and use the invoices for nothing else. The match never sets an event amount, which comes from Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses (REQ-008; Q-042). Invoice lines are at ledger-distribution grain (RULE-104): a readmission fee split across several lines is one fee, and an invoice is counted once, never once per line (RULE-105). Anomalies are limited to the Campaign Years the invoice source covers (review change 11). Anomaly type names are proposals and the design confirms them.

business_rules.rule: The anomaly types in this requirement are raised only for amount Campaign Years the invoice source covers (2022 onward). Events and invoices from earlier years raise none.

For the checks in this requirement, and only for them, each Join, Renewal and Readmission event is matched to its own eligible invoice (RULE-014) for its contact in its amount Campaign Year (RULE-032). Within one contact and amount Campaign Year, the events are ordered by event date and the eligible invoices by trans_date, then paired in that order: the earliest event takes the earliest invoice, the next event the next invoice, and so on (Q-022). The match never sets an event amount (Q-042).

Where a contact and amount Campaign Year has more events than eligible invoices, the invoices go to events in priority order: Readmission, then Renewal, then Join, then the earliest event date. Among the events that receive one, invoices are paired by date (RULE-084). Every other event gets no invoice. This fallback exists only to stop one invoice being matched to two events.

Where a contact and amount Campaign Year has more eligible invoices than events, the events are paired by date with the latest invoices by trans_date. The earlier surplus invoices are matched to no event (Q-022).
No eligible invoice is matched to more than one event.

Mike runs them on real data and brings the results back as answers, and the agents' tests run them on synthetic data. They cover: the CUSTTRANS_RICS grain profile (Q-021, review change 1); corporate subscription status values (Q-027); payment method coverage; invoiced subtotal coverage and amount_status counts; the Direct Debit share of Partially Paid positions; and totals by payment method, payer type and concession for the last full Campaign Year. business_rules.rule: Every query returns aggregates only (counts, sums, rates), never contact-level rows or contact identifiers.

The grain profile groups synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS invoice rows (TRANSTYPE not 8 or 24, invoice number not containing 'CRE' or 'FTCN') by ACCOUNTNUM and INVOICE. It returns the number of invoices by rows per invoice, by distinct productcode per invoice, and by whether the invoice has a row whose PostingType_Description contains 'tax'. The corporate status profile returns row counts of Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions by 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' value.

Payment method coverage is the share of paid positions whose payment method is one of the five methods (payment_method_id above 0), by Campaign Year from 2021. It is also reported by event type, so Change and Lapse events are checked on their own.
Invoiced subtotal coverage is the share of Join, Renewal and Readmission events with a non-null invoiced_subtotal_gbp, by Campaign Year, with event counts by amount_status.

requirements.title: Derived retirement date drives Practising / Retired
requirements.description: apuk_retirementdate is entered by hand and is not always trustworthy. Each contact therefore gets a derived retirement date: the payment date of their first invoice that carries a retired concession, taken from Subs.vwSubsMemberStatuses as landed in Layercake.brnz_subs_status (REQ-002). It replaces apuk_retirementdate (Layercake.silv_member_base.retirement_date) everywhere that date drives Practising / Retired: events, annual rates and daily counts (Mike, AMD-001, 2026-11-06; supersedes Q-009). As a result, Phase 1 results split by membership status change. Apart from region and country (REQ-027), no other Phase 1 result changes (Q-046). Past daily counts take the new split on the next daily run, with no one-off rebuild (REQ-018, AMD-003). The design names the object that holds the derived date.

business_rules.rule: A contact's derived retirement date is the 'Renewal Date' on the contact's live brnz_subs_status row (_is_deleted = 0) with the earliest Campaign Year whose 'Retired Concession' is 'Retired Conc.' and whose 'Renewal Date' is not null (Q-041). In the owner's source, 'Retired Conc.' means at least one of the contact-year's invoices that is not fully credited carries one of the six retired item codes (RULE-055). 'Renewal Date' is the contact-year's first payment date. For a Full Concession invoice it is the date the concession settled the invoice, kept inside the Campaign Year. A contact with no such row has no derived retirement date.

Wherever Phase 1 sets Practising / Retired from Layercake.silv_member_base.retirement_date, it uses the derived retirement date instead. That covers silv_membership_events and fact_membership_events, silv_annual_rate_base and fact_annual_rate_base, silv_daily_count_detail and fact_daily_member_count_detail. The contact is Retired from that date, inclusive. The rest of the status logic is unchanged.

There is no fallback to apuk_retirementdate or to 'First Retired Year'. A contact with no derived retirement date is never Retired because of a retirement date. A member who retired before Campaign Year 2022 is therefore Practising until their first retired-concession year from 2022 onward (Q-040).

requirements.title: Past daily counts kept in line with silver on every run
requirements.description: Today Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count derives a past date once and never again unless someone runs usp_load_silver @RebuildFrom or @FullRebuild, while the silver it reads is re-derived on every run, so stored daily history drifts away from it (Mike, AMD-003, 2026-11-17). requirements.title: Adjustment history of daily counts
requirements.description: Mike wants a history of adjustments kept in an easy format, so that the numbers on a particular day can be worked out when needed (AMD-003, 2026-11-17). A new Layercake table (name set by the design) keeps one row for each daily count cell whose numbers changed, for each run that changed it, at the grain of silv_daily_count_detail. Each row holds the run, when it was written, the date and grain columns, and the change (new minus old) for each of the seven daily measures. The catch-up done by the first run after deployment is recorded like any other run, so the size of the drift up to now can be read from it. The history covers the daily count measures only. It is kept indefinitely.

business_rules.rule: The adjustment history holds one row per daily count cell per run that changed any of the cell's seven daily measures. The cell is ([date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id and, from AMD-008, local_group_id and contact_country_id, with the own-country region carried alongside, RULE-176). Each row holds the run_id, the time it was written, the date and grain columns, and new minus old for active_count, paid_count, paid_count_event, event_join_count, event_renewal_count, event_readmission_count and event_lapse_count. A measure the run did not change holds 0. A cell whose seven measures are all unchanged gets no row. Rows written before AMD-007 was deployed hold -2 Not applicable in payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id (RULE-162). Rows written before AMD-008 was deployed hold the values set out in RULE-179.
Where a cell has no row in silv_daily_count_detail before or after the change, its figures on that side count as 0.

The first load of a date that has never been loaded is not an adjustment and writes no row. Repeat loads of today (today is rebuilt on every run) are adjustments like any other and write rows for the cells they change.

Every change to stored daily counts is recorded, whichever path makes it: the scheduled usp_run_daily_load, including the first run after deployment, or a manual usp_load_silver @RebuildFrom or @FullRebuild. The row carries the run_id of that run or call.

The history holds every committed change and never holds a change that was rolled back. For every cell and measure, the figure stored after any run equals the figure stored before it plus the sum of the adjustment rows that run wrote.
The adjustment history is kept indefinitely. Nothing purges it.

The history covers the seven daily measures of silv_daily_count_detail only. Changes to segment or amount columns on events, and to the annual rate base, write no adjustment row of their own. A change to a contact's attributes writes adjustment rows only for the daily count cells it moves the contact out of and into (REQ-026).

requirements.title: Daily counts as known at any time, and adjustments review
requirements.description: The figure for any date, as it stood at time T, is today's stored figure minus the adjustments written after T (Mike, AMD-003, 2026-11-17). A view or function in Layercake gives these figures for a date range and a time T, at the silv_daily_count grain and at the detail grain, so nobody has to write the subtraction by hand. A second view lists the adjustments by date, run and measure for review. The history starts with the first run after deployment, so for a time T before that run the figures are those stored just before it. Object names and the interface are set by the design.

business_rules.rule: The figure for a date, cell and measure as it stood at time T is the figure stored today in silv_daily_count_detail minus the sum of that cell's adjustment changes written after T (assumes Q-049 for the clock and the boundary at T). A cell with no stored row today counts as 0 before the subtraction, so a cell removed after T still shows its figure at T.

A Layercake view or function returns the figures as known at T for a date range (from and to dates inclusive) and a time T, for all seven daily measures. It works at two grains. The detail grain is ([date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id and, from AMD-008, local_group_id and contact_country_id, RULE-176). The silv_daily_count grain is ([date], region, grade). At the silv_daily_count grain the figures are the detail-grain figures summed over every detail grain column other than [date], region and grade.
For a date first loaded after T, the figures returned are its first-load figures, following RULE-119 literally (assumes Q-050).

A second Layercake view lists the adjustments for review by date, run and measure: one row per cell, run and measure with a non-zero change, with the cell's grain columns, the run_id, the time written, the measure name and the change (assumes Q-051).

requirements.title: One corporate subscription row per contact, scheme and Campaign Year
requirements.description: The first production run of Layercake.usp_run_daily_load after MIG-0023 to MIG-0025 failed in Layercake.usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription with error 2627, because Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions repeated a (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year) key in Campaign Year 2027. Phase 1 and the two invoice bronze loads committed, the corporate subscription table was left unchanged and the later segment loads did not run (Mike, AMD-004, 2026-11-18). The view is at subscription-user grain (CE.vwRicsv2Subscription joined to CE.vwSubscriptionUser), and a contact can hold several subscription-user records on one subscription and Campaign Year, for example removed in one round and added again in a later one. Production holds repeated keys in every Campaign Year from 2022 to 2027 (2027: 563 keys, up to 4 rows per key). Within a repeated key only the subscription-user columns (Round, Sub User State, Sub User Status, Sub User Created Date) differ, 14 keys repeat identical rows, and no key has more than one copy with Sub Status and Sub User Status both 'Active'. This answers the design's Q-033 (No) and replaces the behaviour built on it, where a repeated key failed the load. The load now lands one row per key, chosen in a fixed order, and a repeat is neither an error nor a data anomaly. The readers of the table are not changed. AMD-005 (2026-11-18) changes RULE-130 for a NULL 'Sub Campaign Year' only: such a row is skipped and counted instead of failing the load (REQ-023).

business_rules.rule: Layercake.usp_load_brnz_corporate_subscription lands one row per (Contact No, Scheme No, Sub Campaign Year) of Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions. Where the source holds several rows for a key, it keeps, in this order: (1) the copy whose 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' are both the active value ('Active', assumes Q-027); then (2) the copy with the latest 'Sub User Created Date', where a copy with a NULL date loses to every copy that has a date (Q-053); then (3) the copy with the highest 'Round', compared by the whole number at its end (the digits after the last space, so 'Round 10' beats 'Round 9'), never as text and never cast whole, where a NULL Round or one that does not end in a whole number counts as lowest (Q-053). Any remaining tie, including identical rows, is broken deterministically, so the same source data always lands the same row. The exact final tie-break is the design's decision.

A repeated key is not an error and does not fail the load. It is not a data anomaly: no Layercake.silv_data_anomaly row is written for it. Every run logs the number of source rows not landed as repeats (source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year minus their distinct keys), including 0 when no key repeats. A row with a NULL Sub Campaign Year is never counted as a repeat; it is counted under RULE-135 instead. How it is logged is the design's decision, for example a Layercake.etl_progress_log sub-step.

A source row with a NULL 'Contact No' or 'Scheme No' still fails the load with error 515; the load logs Failed, re-raises and leaves brnz_corporate_subscription unchanged (Mike, 2026-10-26). A row with a NULL 'Sub Campaign Year' no longer fails the load: it is skipped and counted (REQ-023; Mike, AMD-005, 2026-11-18). 'Round' is still not landed and plays no part except as the tie-break in RULE-128 (Mike, 2026-10-23). The row-count check (RULE-005) compares the number of distinct keys among the source rows that have a Sub Campaign Year with the live bronze rows.

The readers of brnz_corporate_subscription are not changed: Layercake.usp_load_silv_member_year_attributes, Layercake.usp_load_silv_data_anomaly_segment and the three employer reports of REQ-013 (Layercake.usp_report_employer_scheme_coverage, Layercake.usp_report_employer_source_agreement and Layercake.usp_report_top_employers). Each asks only whether a live row with both statuses active exists for the contact and Campaign Year, and RULE-128 lands such a row whenever the source holds one for the key.

Recovery after deployment needs no manual cleanup: running Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments once, or letting the next Layercake.usp_run_daily_load run, lands the corporate subscriptions and runs the segment loads that did not run, because every segment load applies only differences.

The handover is updated: docs/handover/06-known-limitations.md (the Q-033 entry, and the limitation that one incomplete or repeated corporate subscription row stops the whole load) and the runbook (docs/handover/04-runbook.md).

requirements.title: Daily count recomputes only the contacts that changed
requirements.description: Mike asked for a faster daily load (AMD-006, 2026-11-19). In production Layercake.usp_run_daily_load took 70 minutes at 06:00 and 39 minutes at 08:20 on 2026-11-19, of which Layercake.usp_load_silv_daily_count took 50 and 32 minutes. The last four daily count runs all corrected the whole spine from 2020-10-01 (2,241 dates), because a contact's earliest affected date is the start of the Campaign Year of the contact's earliest input row ever, while only 394 of 178,751 contacts changed at 08:20 (67 at 06:00). From this change, a normal run of usp_load_silv_daily_count recomputes only the contacts whose inputs changed and the dates those inputs reach, using the fact that the count rule is additive per contact. The results do not change: the tables and the adjustment history are exactly what the current method gives (REQ-018 to REQ-020 unchanged). The full recompute stays for @FullRebuild, @RebuildFrom and changed reference tables. How a changed contact's old contribution is known and how an emptied cell is recognised and removed are the design's decisions. The speed target is the one real-data check in this release: a human checks it on production at handover, and the agents' tests set no time limit (Q-057). Q-026 still holds for data results.

business_rules.rule: On a normal run (no @FullRebuild, no @RebuildFrom and no reference table change, RULE-147), usp_load_silv_daily_count recomputes only the contacts whose inputs (their rows in Layercake.silv_membership_events, silv_member_state_ranges, silv_payment_events, silv_member_profile and, from AMD-007, silv_member_year_attributes, RULE-160) changed since they were last applied, and only for the dates their old and new inputs reach. The work done is proportional to the changed contacts and those dates, not to the whole spine. Dates never loaded before, including the run date on its first run, are first-loaded as today and write no adjustment rows (RULE-114).

Speed target: on a normal day (no more than 394 changed contacts, the 08:20 run of 2026-11-19), the usp_load_silv_daily_count step takes under 5 minutes and the whole usp_run_daily_load run takes under 15 minutes, measured on a run that does not overlap Subs.usp_Subs_Refresh_Data. A human checks it on production from Layercake.etl_run_log, on a normal run after the first post-deployment run, as a listed handover step. If it is missed, the human records the timings and the logged count (RULE-153) and raises it with Mike; it is not a reason to roll back (Q-057).

Results do not change. After any run, silv_daily_count_detail, silv_daily_count and fact_daily_member_count_detail are identical to what @FullRebuild = 1 produces on the same data (for the fact, every column except id). The adjustment history holds exactly the rows the current method would write: the same cells, the same new-minus-old changes, and no rows for first loads. REQ-018, REQ-019 and REQ-020 still hold in full: the whole spine from 2020-10-01, no closed-year freeze, every measure and every cause, and the 'as known at' objects and adjustments review view unchanged.

The count rule is additive per contact: on any day a contact sits in at most one daily count cell, so each of the seven daily measures in a cell is the sum of its contacts' contributions. The design may rely on this.

usp_load_silv_daily_count fails with a clear error, writing nothing, if any contact holds two overlapping non-zero-length ranges in Layercake.silv_member_state_ranges. A range covers [valid_from, valid_to), with a NULL valid_to open-ended. It is non-zero-length when valid_to is NULL or later than valid_from. Two non-zero-length ranges of one contact overlap when each starts before the other ends. Ranges that meet (one's valid_to equals the next's valid_from) do not overlap, and a zero-length range never overlaps (Q-055). The check applies on every path, normal or full.

The full recompute stays: usp_load_silver @FullRebuild = 1 and @RebuildFrom keep working as today, and may use the faster count form. Their changes are written to the adjustment history as today (RULE-115).

A changed reference table (Layercake.ref_date_spine, Layercake.ref_campaign_year_config or Layercake.silv_ref_membership_status) still makes the run recompute the whole spine. Only reference rows up to the latest date already marked in Layercake.etl_daily_count_loaded count: ref_date_spine rows dated from 2020-10-01 to that date, ref_campaign_year_config rows whose campaign_year_start is on or before that date, and silv_ref_membership_status in full. The routine extension of ref_date_spine with dates after the latest loaded date, and the addition of a Campaign Year that starts after the latest loaded date, are not a change for this rule.

The first run after deployment may run a full recompute to set up whatever the new method stores. That run writes no adjustment rows if the stored figures are already right, and otherwise records the drift as RULE-109 and RULE-115 say.

Failure and resume are as today: a run that fails part way re-raises the error, and the next run resumes with no manual cleanup, recomputing every contact whose change was not applied. The adjustment history never holds a change that was rolled back (RULE-111, RULE-116).

Every run of usp_load_silv_daily_count logs the number of contacts it recomputed, including 0, and whether it took the full-recompute path (@FullRebuild, @RebuildFrom or a reference table change). How it is logged is the design's decision, for example a Layercake.etl_progress_log sub-step (as RULE-129 and RULE-135).

The existing MOD-021 and MOD-022 parity tests keep passing. New tests show that the changed-contacts path gives exactly the same tables and adjustment rows as a full recompute, for at least: a new contact, a removed contact, a backdated enrolment, a lapse, a renewal, a country or gender change (which moves a member's whole history), a retirement date change, a contact moving cell, and a cell that empties.

Starting each time from the same fully loaded synthetic state, each of these source changes is made on its own, and usp_run_daily_load runs with no @RebuildFrom or @FullRebuild: (a) new contact N1 with a Join dated 2023-05-10; (b) contact R1, active from 2021-01-15, removed from the source; (c) a backdated enrolment for E1 dated 2021-02-01 (AC-024-04); (d) a Lapse for L1 dated 2024-02-10; (e) a Renewal for D1 dated 2025-01-10 (AC-018-01); (f) G1's country_id changed from 1 to 2 (AC-024-05), and separately G2's gender_id changed from 1 to 2; (g) T5's derived retirement date changed from 2025-01-15 to 2024-12-01 (AC-018-03); (h) contact V1 moving from grade 'enrolment' to 'election' on 2023-09-01; (i) cell E emptying (AC-024-06). After each run, silv_daily_count_detail and silv_daily_count equal the result of usp_load_silver @FullRebuild = 1 on the same data, and fact_daily_member_count_detail equals the full recompute followed by the gold load in every column except id: 0 rows differ, 0 missing, 0 extra. The adjustment rows the run wrote equal, cell by cell and measure by measure, the stored silv_daily_count_detail figures after the run minus before it, for every date loaded before the run, with no row whose seven changes are all 0 and no row for a date first loaded by the run: 0 mismatches.

Contact E1 has no inputs, and every date from 2020-10-01 to the run date is loaded. A backdated enrolment for E1 dated 2021-02-01 is added. After the next usp_run_daily_load, active_count in E1's cell is 1 higher on 2021-02-01 and on the run date and unchanged on 2021-01-31. Every adjustment row the run wrote is in E1's cell, dated 2021-02-01 or later, with an active_count change of +1, and the run logs 1 contact recomputed and the normal path.

Contact G1 is active in grade 'election', Practising, country_id 1, gender_id 1, on every date from 2020-10-01 to the run date, and every such date is loaded. Only G1's country_id changes, to 2. After the next usp_run_daily_load, on every loaded date active_count is 1 lower in G1's country_id 1 cell and 1 higher in its country_id 2 cell. The run writes exactly 2 adjustment rows per loaded date, with active_count changes of -1 and +1 (other measures as AC-024-03 requires), and logs 1 contact recomputed and the normal path.

Cell E (2022-03-01, region 'UK', country_id 3, gender_id 2, grade 'election', membership_status_id 1, with M1's 2022 payment method, payer type and concession type) holds only contact M1, with active_count 1. M1's country_id changes to 4. After the next usp_run_daily_load, neither silv_daily_count_detail nor fact_daily_member_count_detail holds a row for cell E with a non-zero measure, and both hold for 2022-03-01 exactly the rows the full recompute produces. The run writes an adjustment row for cell E on 2022-03-01 with an active_count change of -1.

Contact S9 has two ranges in silv_member_state_ranges: valid_from 2023-01-01 with valid_to NULL, and valid_from 2024-01-01 with valid_to 2024-06-01. usp_load_silv_daily_count fails and re-raises an error, logs 'Failed' with an error_message naming the contact (S9), and leaves silv_daily_count_detail, silv_daily_count, the adjustment history and Layercake.etl_daily_count_loaded exactly as they were. The same holds for usp_load_silver @FullRebuild = 1 (assumes Q-055).

Contact S10 has ranges valid_from 2023-01-01 to valid_to 2024-01-01 and valid_from 2024-01-01 with valid_to NULL. Contact S11 has a range valid_from 2023-01-01 with valid_to NULL and a zero-length range valid_from 2024-03-01, valid_to 2024-03-01. With S10 and S11 in the synthetic set and no S9, usp_load_silv_daily_count logs 'Success' (assumes Q-055).

usp_load_silver @FullRebuild = 1, and separately @RebuildFrom = '2025-01-01', each log that the daily count took the full-recompute path and leave AC-018-02's comparison with 0 differences. After a column of an existing row is changed, in turn, in ref_date_spine (a date from 2020-10-01 to the run date), ref_campaign_year_config (Campaign Year 2023) and silv_ref_membership_status, the next usp_run_daily_load logs the full-recompute path and leaves AC-018-02's comparison with 0 differences.

The synthetic set is loaded by the procedures as they are before this change, with no source change since that load. From this change, the fact is synced from silver at cell level: changed cells are updated, new cells inserted and cells no longer in silver deleted, and unchanged cells and dates are not touched. The final row-count check against silver stays. The id column is widened to bigint, so it cannot run out (Q-056).

Rows for unchanged cells, and for dates with no changed cell, are not touched.
The final row-count check of the fact against silver stays.
fact_daily_member_count_detail.id is widened from int to bigint and kept (Q-056). How it is widened is the design's decision.

requirements.description: Mike, 2026-11-20 (AMD-007): 'We need to update the fact fact_daily_member_count_detail to add the new segmentation for payer type, payment method and concession. It will increase the row count, but that's fine.' Today Layercake.fact_daily_member_count_detail is at the grain date x country x gender x membership grade x membership status. Each contact's payment method, payer type and concession type are held per contact and Campaign Year in Layercake.silv_member_year_attributes and reach only the event tables, and Layercake.usp_run_daily_load runs the daily count before the attributes of the same run are loaded. From this change the daily count detail, its adjustment history, its cell counts, the detail 'as known at' function, the adjustments review view and the gold daily fact gain payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id in their grain. A contact-day takes the values of its attributes row for the Campaign Year of the day. The seven measures and every total at the old grain stay exactly as they are, and Layercake.silv_daily_count keeps its grain. The run loads the attributes before the daily count, the changed-contacts path (REQ-024) treats an attribute change like any other input change, and the gold fact is synced cell by cell on the new key (REQ-025). This answers Q-007 for the daily count; the annual rate base keeps its grain.

business_rules.rule: Layercake.silv_daily_count_detail gains payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id (silver ids, never null) in its grain, which becomes ([date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id). Layercake.fact_daily_member_count_detail gains the same three columns (int not null, keys of dim_payment_method, dim_payer_type and dim_concession_type), and they join the star grain and its unique clustered index. The same three columns join the grain of Layercake.silv_daily_count_adjustment, Layercake.etl_daily_count_cell_contacts, Layercake.fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at and Layercake.vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review. Layercake.silv_daily_count and Layercake.fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at keep their grain and their figures. From AMD-008, local_group_id and contact_country_id also join the grain of each of these detail-grain objects, with the own-country region carried alongside (REQ-027, RULE-176).

A contact-day takes payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id from the contact's silv_member_year_attributes row for the Campaign Year of the day, for every grade (enrolment, election and lapse) and for every measure counted for the contact that day (assumes Q-060). Carried values count as the value: the payment_method_carried, payer_type_carried and concession_type_carried flags are not part of the grain. A contact-day with no attributes row takes 0 Unknown for all three, as silv_membership_events does. Before 2022 the attributes hold -2 Not applicable (RULE-080), and that value is used. Corporate account (employer) is not added.

The seven daily measures keep their rules. Every total at the old detail grain (summed over payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id), and every figure of silv_daily_count, stays exactly what it is without this change. On any day a contact still sits in one cell, because the attributes are one row per contact and Campaign Year, so the additive count rule (RULE-144) still holds.

The daily count uses the attributes as loaded earlier in the same Layercake.usp_run_daily_load run: the run loads silv_member_year_attributes before the daily count. The exact order is the design's decision. A failure anywhere still fails the run and is re-raised, and the next run recovers with no manual step (RULE-125).
Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments stays callable on its own (RULE-126). If it is run on its own and changes attributes, the next usp_run_daily_load brings the daily count into line.

A change to a contact's attributes (payment_method_id, payer_type_id or concession_type_id, in any Campaign Year) makes that contact a changed contact, so the changed-contacts path (RULE-141) recomputes it like any other input change, and the result stays identical to @FullRebuild = 1 (RULE-143). A changed attribute moves that contact's days of that Campaign Year from one cell to another, which writes adjustment rows like a country or gender change does.

A change to Layercake.silv_ref_payment_method, silv_ref_payer_type or silv_ref_concession_type does not by itself make the daily count take the full-recompute path, because the ids are carried from the attributes, not derived from these lists.

On deployment, silv_daily_count_detail, fact_daily_member_count_detail and etl_daily_count_cell_contacts are restated at the new grain (the first run after deployment may take the full-recompute path to do it, and to set up whatever the changed-contacts snapshot now stores). The restatement is a change of grain, not of numbers, and writes no adjustment rows. Adjustment rows written before the deployment keep their figures and take -2 Not applicable in payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id, because the segment was not recorded then.
'As known at' a time before the deployment is exact at the silv_daily_count grain and at the old detail grain (summed over the three new columns), but is not split by segment.

The gold cell-by-cell sync (RULE-150, RULE-151) uses the eight-column key (date_id, country_id, gender_id, membership_grade_id, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id, concession_type_id). From AMD-008 the key also includes local_group_id and contact_country_id (RULE-176). The sync updates changed cells, inserts new cells, deletes cells no longer in silver and does not touch unchanged cells. The final row-count check against silver stays. id stays bigint (RULE-152). No foreign keys are added for the three new columns, as on the segment columns of fact_membership_events.

The migration and its rollback are safe to run on production outside the 06:00 run, create no schema and work in the existing Layercake schema. The migration comes after MIG-0028 and MIG-0029, which may not yet be on production.

Downstream readers are checked and changed where the grain matters. Check D2 of reference/phase1/Scripts/Reconciliation/pipeline-reconciliation-report.sql rebuilds the expected star from silver, so it gains the three columns. active-member-difference.sql and paid-member-difference.sql only sum by date, so AMD-007 does not change them, but they are re-checked. From AMD-008, the difference scripts are re-baselined where region is involved, and D2 also gains local_group_id and contact_country_id (RULE-181).

The handover (docs/handover/02-architecture.md, 03-data-lineage.md, 04-runbook.md, 06-known-limitations.md and 07-glossary.md) describes the new grain and says that any report reading fact_daily_member_count_detail must sum over payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id. The known limitations say that 'as known at' a time before the deployment is not split by segment (RULE-163).

The MOD-021, MOD-022, MOD-026 and MOD-027 tests keep passing, changed only where they name the grain. New tests show at least: a contact-day takes the attributes of the day's Campaign Year (a contact whose method changes between years splits across cells at 1 October); no attributes row gives 0; before 2022 gives -2; an attribute change alone is picked up by the changed-contacts path and gives exactly the @FullRebuild result and adjustment rows; totals at the old grain are unchanged by the new columns; gold carries the dim keys and syncs cell by cell on the new key.

Same attributes row as payment_method_id (RULE-156). 0 where no row matches. Part of the grain.
Same attributes row as payment_method_id (RULE-156). 0 where no row matches. Part of the grain.

Copy. Equals the dim_payer_type key. int not null; part of the star grain and the unique clustered index; no foreign key (RULE-155, RULE-164).
Copy. Equals the dim_concession_type key. int not null; part of the star grain and the unique clustered index; no foreign key (RULE-155, RULE-164).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: After deployment, silv_daily_count_detail and fact_daily_member_count_detail each have exactly their earlier columns plus payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id, all not null (int on the fact), and the AMD-008 columns of REQ-027. silv_daily_count_adjustment, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts, vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review and the result of fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at each gain the same three columns. The unique clustered index of fact_daily_member_count_detail covers exactly date_id, country_id, gender_id, membership_grade_id, membership_status_id, payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id, and from AMD-008 also local_group_id and contact_country_id (RULE-176). No foreign key is defined on the fact's three new columns, and id is still bigint. The column list of silv_daily_count and the result columns of fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at are unchanged.

Contact Y1 is active in grade 'election', Practising, region 'UK', country_id 1, gender_id 1, from 2023-10-01 onward, and dates 2024-09-01 to 2025-03-31 are loaded. Contact Y2 is active in grade 'election' on 2025-01-10 and has no silv_member_year_attributes row for any Campaign Year. In silv_daily_count_detail and fact_daily_member_count_detail, Y2 is counted on 2025-01-10 in a cell with payment_method_id 0, payer_type_id 0 and concession_type_id 0.

Contact Y3 is active in grade 'election' on 2021-05-01, and Y3's 2021 attributes row holds -2 for payment method, payer type and concession type. Y3 is counted on 2021-05-01 in a cell with payment_method_id -2, payer_type_id -2 and concession_type_id -2 (assumes Q-011).

Contacts Y4 and Y5 are active in grade 'election', Practising, region 'UK', country_id 1, gender_id 1, on 2025-11-01 (Campaign Year 2026), and are the only contacts there. On 2025-11-01 both are counted in one cell with active_count 2. Neither silv_daily_count_detail nor fact_daily_member_count_detail has a payment_method_carried, payer_type_carried or concession_type_carried column.

Contact Y6 is in grade 'enrolment' on 2025-01-10 with 2025 attributes of payment method Corporate, payer type Corporate and No concession, and is counted on that date in the cell with those three ids. Contact Y7's Lapse dated 2025-06-01 is counted (event_lapse_count 1) on 2025-06-01 in the cell with Y7's 2025 attributes, payment method Card.

Contact Y8 has a Join dated 2024-06-01 (Campaign Year 2024) and a first paid position in Campaign Year 2025, with attributes 2024: Card and 2025: Direct Debit. In silv_daily_count_detail on 2024-06-01, Y8's active_count and event_join_count are both in the cell with the Card id, and in no other cell. In fact_membership_events, Y8's Join carries Direct Debit (RULE-017) (assumes Q-060).

On the same synthetic source data, compare the result before and after the change. silv_daily_count_detail summed over payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id equals silv_daily_count_detail before the change, matching on [date], region, country_id, gender_id, grade and membership_status_id: 0 rows differ in any of the seven measures, 0 missing, 0 extra. silv_daily_count is identical: 0 differences. fact_daily_member_count_detail summed over the three new columns equals the fact before the change on (date_id, country_id, gender_id, membership_grade_id, membership_status_id): 0 differences.

From a fully loaded synthetic state, the payment mode of Y1's 2025 segment invoice in Subs.tblSubsInvoices changes from Card to DD, and nothing else in the source changes. After one call of usp_run_daily_load, with no @RebuildFrom or @FullRebuild and no second run: (a) the silv_member_year_attributes step row under that run_id has status 'Success' and a finished_at no later than the started_at of the usp_load_silv_daily_count step row; (b) usp_load_silv_daily_count logs 1 contact recomputed and the normal path; (c) on every loaded date from 2024-10-01 to 2025-03-31, Y1 is counted in the Direct Debit cell and not in the Card cell, and Y1's cells on dates up to 2024-09-30 are unchanged; (d) silv_daily_count_detail and silv_daily_count equal the result of usp_load_silver @FullRebuild = 1 on the same data, and fact_daily_member_count_detail equals the full recompute followed by the gold load in every column except id: 0 rows differ, 0 missing, 0 extra; (e) silv_daily_count is unchanged by the run.

For each loaded date from 2024-10-01 to 2025-03-31, the run in AC-026-09 writes one adjustment row for Y1's Card cell with active_count_change -1 and one for Y1's Direct Debit cell with active_count_change +1, with the other measures as the stored figures require. Each row carries its cell's actual payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id, not -2. The run writes no adjustment row dated before 2024-10-01. For every cell and measure, the run's changes equal the stored figure after the run minus before it: 0 mismatches. Summed to the silv_daily_count grain, the run's changes are 0 for every measure.

Starting each time from the same fully loaded synthetic state: (a) contact Y10's 2023 segment invoice gains an Exceptional Hardship concession line, which changes only Y10's 2023 concession_type_id, from No concession to Exceptional Hardship; (b) contact Y11, whose 2025 segment invoice has payment mode Corporate and who has a 2025 paid position, gains a 2025 corporate subscription row with Sub Status and Sub User Status 'Active', which changes only Y11's 2025 payer_type_id, from Individual to Corporate. After one usp_run_daily_load, each case logs 1 contact recomputed and the normal path. Y10's loaded dates from 2022-10-01 to 2023-09-30, and Y11's loaded dates in Campaign Year 2025, move to the cell with the new id. The comparison in AC-026-09 (d) shows 0 differences (assumes Q-002, Q-027).

A new concession type is added to the source concession reference. This adds one row to silv_ref_concession_type and dim_concession_type and changes no contact's attributes. The next usp_run_daily_load logs 0 contacts recomputed and the normal path for usp_load_silv_daily_count, writes 0 adjustment rows, and changes no row of silv_daily_count_detail, silv_daily_count or fact_daily_member_count_detail.

After a successful usp_run_daily_load, the AC-026-09 source change is made, and Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments is called on its own, which changes Y1's 2025 attributes row to Direct Debit. The next usp_run_daily_load, with no manual step, logs 1 contact recomputed and the normal path, counts Y1 in the Direct Debit cell on every loaded date from 2024-10-01, and leaves the comparison in AC-026-09 (d) with 0 differences.

The AC-026-09 source change is made, and Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions holds a row whose 'Contact No' is NULL. usp_run_daily_load fails, re-raises error 515 to the caller, and its run row in etl_run_log has status 'Failed'. After the row is corrected, the next usp_run_daily_load, with no manual cleanup, ends 'Success', counts Y1 in the Direct Debit cell on every loaded date from 2024-10-01, and leaves the comparison in AC-026-09 (d) with 0 differences.

On the synthetic set after usp_run_daily_load, no fact_daily_member_count_detail row has a null payment_method_id, payer_type_id or concession_type_id, and every value resolves to a row of dim_payment_method, dim_payer_type and dim_concession_type respectively: 0 orphans. Matching each silv_daily_count_detail cell to the fact through the existing gold keys for date, country, gender, grade and status and the three new ids, the fact holds exactly the silver cells with the same seven measures: 0 differ, 0 missing, 0 extra. The gold load's row-count check against silver passes.

In the AC-026-09 run, every fact_daily_member_count_detail row whose grain key (RULE-164) has the same figures before and after keeps its id and all its values. The gold load's rows_updated, rows_inserted and rows_deleted equal the number of fact cells, on the grain key, whose figures changed, that are new and that are gone. A fact row is then added by hand that matches a silver cell in every grain column except payment_method_id. The next usp_run_daily_load deletes it, logs 'Success' for usp_load_fact_daily_member_count_detail with the row-count check passing, and changes no other fact row.

The synthetic set is loaded by the procedures as they are before this change, over at least three runs that write adjustment rows. The migration is applied, and then the first usp_run_daily_load runs with no source change since the last load. The migration and that run write 0 adjustment rows. Every adjustment row written before the deployment is still present with the same run_id, written_at, date, old grain columns and seven changes, and holds -2 in payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id. silv_daily_count is identical to before: 0 differences. Summed over the three new columns, silv_daily_count_detail (seven measures), etl_daily_count_cell_contacts (contact_count) and fact_daily_member_count_detail equal their contents before the deployment on the old grain: 0 differences. silv_daily_count_detail, silv_daily_count and fact_daily_member_count_detail (except id) equal the result of usp_load_silver @FullRebuild = 1 and the gold load on the same data: 0 differences.

In AC-026-17, take a time T between two of the pre-deployment runs and the date range 2020-10-01 to the run date. After the deployment, fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at returns exactly the figures it returned for the same T and range before the deployment: 0 differences. fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at, summed over the three new columns, returns exactly the figures the detail function returned before the deployment: 0 differences.

migrations.py check passes, and migrations.py roundtrip passes for the migration of this change. Its MIG number is higher than MIG-0029, it creates no schema, and every object it creates or changes is in the Layercake schema.

After one usp_run_daily_load on the test database loaded with the synthetic data, check D2 of reference/phase1/Scripts/Reconciliation/pipeline-reconciliation-report.sql compares fact_daily_member_count_detail with the star it rebuilds from silver, including payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id, and reports no difference. active-member-difference.sql and paid-member-difference.sql both read PASS. They are unchanged by AMD-007; from AMD-008 they are re-baselined for region (RULE-181).

docs/handover/02-architecture.md, 03-data-lineage.md, 04-runbook.md, 06-known-limitations.md and 07-glossary.md each describe the grain of fact_daily_member_count_detail including payment_method_id, payer_type_id and concession_type_id. Each states that any report reading the fact must sum over those three columns. 06-known-limitations.md states that adjustment rows written before the deployment hold -2 in the three columns, so 'as known at' a time before the deployment is not split by segment.

After the change, every test in the MOD-021, MOD-022, MOD-026 and MOD-027 tSQLt suites passes. Each test differs from its version before the change only where it names the grain of the daily detail tables, the adjustment history, the cell counts, the 'as known at' functions, the review view or the gold fact.

requirements.title: Member country and region by local group
requirements.description: Mike, 2026-11-26 (AMD-008): 'the decision is to add a new dimension but feed the values into the existing fields - so that PBI does not need to change ... The old values can be kept but added as a new column where necessary.' Then: 'BR-001 can be overridden ... Region can change. Greater rows and grain is fine.' The business's paid membership by region on 30 Sep 2026 (the Subs paid and Member Demographics figures) does not match Layercake by region, although both sides count the same 141,224 paid contacts. Layercake gives a member a region from the member's own country (CE.vwContact.rics_countryid). The business figures give a member a region from the member's local group (CE.vwContact.rics_localgroupid, through CE.vwLocalGroup). About 2,000 paid members have a local group in a different region from their country, for example members whose country is the United Kingdom, India or Sri Lanka in Gulf local groups. A production check reproduced the business figures from the local group to within one or two members per region. From this change a member's local group is a reported attribute, a new dimension. The existing country and region fields that reports read today carry the values that follow from the member's local group, so Power BI reports need no change and their regional figures agree with the business's. The values those fields carry today, from the member's own country, are kept and stay reportable in new columns. The scope is everywhere a member's country or region is reported today: the daily member counts, the membership events and the annual rate base, in silver and gold, for every date including closed Campaign Years and anything rebuilt or restated. Region and country figures change, history included. This overrides BR-001's rule that Phase 1 counts by region must not change (REQ-001), and the Phase 1 difference scripts are re-baselined where region is involved. Totals not split by region or country do not change. More rows and a finer grain are accepted. AMD-009 (Mike, 2026-11-26) sets the fallback: a member's local group gives their country and region only when it is usable (RULE-171). Any other member keeps their own country and their own country's region in every field, exactly as today, with local_group_id 0 Unknown, and fields are never mixed. Adjustment rows written before deployment take local_group_id -2 Not applicable, a reserved row of the local group list. Column names marked as proposed are the design's to confirm.

business_rules.rule: Layercake.brnz_contact gains rics_localgroupid, landed 1:1 from CE.vwContact like its existing rics_countryid (RULE-004). CE.vwLocalGroup is landed 1:1 at local group grain, one row per apuk_localgroupid, with the standard bronze audit columns. Whether that is a new bronze table or a change to the Phase 1 Layercake.brnz_local_group is the design's decision. Either way, the own-country region values Phase 1 derives today (silv_ref_country.region_name and market_reporting_region) must stay unchanged.

Layercake.silv_ref_local_group (name proposed) holds one row per local group in CE.vwLocalGroup, plus two reserved rows: 0 Unknown and -2 Not applicable. It is insert-and-update by apuk_localgroupid, as silv_ref_country is: new groups are added, changed values are updated, and existing ids never change. Each row holds the group's name, its code, the silv_ref_country id of its country (apuk_countryid), and its region values apuk_worldregionid_name and Market_reporting_region. An inactive local group (statecode not 0), or one with no country or no region, stays in the list, but it is not usable and gives no member their country or region (RULE-171; Q-063, Q-066). -2 Not applicable is used only on adjustment rows written before deployment (RULE-179); no member is ever given -2. Gold Layercake.dim_local_group (name proposed) is copied from it, including both reserved rows.

A member's local group is usable only when all of these hold: the member has a local group (CE.vwContact.rics_localgroupid is not NULL); CE.vwLocalGroup holds that group; the group is active (statecode 0); it has a country (apuk_countryid is not NULL); and its row gives a region in both region fields (apuk_worldregionid_name and Market_reporting_region are each neither NULL nor blank, blank meaning empty or only spaces). A member whose local group is usable has local_group_id that group's silv_ref_local_group id. Every other member, whichever condition fails, has local_group_id 0 Unknown (Q-062, Q-063, Q-066; Mike, AMD-009). The member's current local group applies to every date of the member's history, including closed Campaign Years (Q-064).

Wherever country_id is held for a member today, it holds the silv_ref_country id of the country of the member's usable local group (CE.vwLocalGroup.apuk_countryid; RULE-171). That covers silv_member_base, silv_member_profile, silv_membership_events, fact_membership_events, silv_annual_rate_base, fact_annual_rate_base, silv_daily_count_detail, fact_daily_member_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts and the daily count adjustment history. A member with no usable local group (local_group_id 0) keeps their own country in country_id, exactly as today (Q-066; Mike, AMD-009).

Every region field that reports read today for a member carries the region of the member's usable local group (RULE-171), as CE.vwLocalGroup gives it for that local group row. These fields are silv_daily_count_detail.region, silv_daily_count.region, and in gold the region_name and market_reporting_region reached from a fact row's country_id through dim_country. Each field keeps the flavour it carries today: the world region field takes apuk_worldregionid_name, and market_reporting_region takes Market_reporting_region, both from the local group row (Q-061). For a usable local group, the row's value wins even where the local group's country gives a different region. A member with no usable local group (local_group_id 0) keeps their own country's value in every region field, exactly as today. There is no field-by-field mixing: a member never takes the local group's region with their own country, or the local group's country with their own region. Either every country and region field follows the usable local group, or every one follows the member's own country (Q-066; Mike, AMD-009). How gold reaches these values is the design's decision, provided reports read them through the same tables and columns as today (RULE-180).

RULE-172 and RULE-173 apply on every date and every path, including closed Campaign Years and anything rebuilt or restated: the normal run, the changed-contacts path, usp_load_silver @FullRebuild and @RebuildFrom, and the full re-derivation of the annual rate base (Q-061).

The values these fields carry today, from the member's own country, are kept. contact_country_id holds the silv_ref_country id of the member's own country (CE.vwContact.rics_countryid), derived exactly as Phase 1 derives country_id today. It is kept wherever country_id is kept for a member (RULE-172). The region from the member's own country is kept alongside it, in the flavour of each region field (Q-061, Q-065). Where a table stores region as a column today (silv_daily_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts, the adjustment history, fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at and vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review), a new own-country region column (named by the design) holds it. Elsewhere it is reached through contact_country_id and silv_ref_country or dim_country.

local_group_id (never null) is carried on every table listed in RULE-172. local_group_id and contact_country_id join the grain wherever country_id is in the grain: silv_daily_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts, the daily count adjustment history, fn_silv_daily_count_detail_as_known_at, vw_silv_daily_count_adjustment_review, fact_daily_member_count_detail and its unique clustered index, silv_annual_rate_base and fact_annual_rate_base (Q-065). The own-country region column is carried alongside contact_country_id. silv_daily_count and fn_silv_daily_count_as_known_at keep their grain ([date], region, grade). In gold, local_group_id is a key of dim_local_group and contact_country_id is a key of dim_country.

Totals not split by region, country or local group do not change: every measure of the daily counts, the events and the annual rate base, summed over region, country_id, local_group_id, contact_country_id and the own-country region, is the same as without this change. The number of events, every event_nk and every event_id are unchanged. Results split by region or country change, history included (Mike, AMD-008).

A change to a member's local group or own country, or to a local group's country, region or status (statecode) in CE.vwLocalGroup, including a change that makes a group usable or not usable (RULE-171), reaches every date of the affected members' history on the next usp_run_daily_load, with no manual step. assumptions: Payment method comes from the invoice's payment mode (Subs.tblSubsInvoices.Inv_Payment_Method), with payment lines from synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS as the fallback. The invoice account number equals the contact number, and the invoice's Campaign Year is used directly (Q-001).

A contact-year is Corporate when its segment invoice has payment method Corporate and the contact is in a live corporate subscription for that year. On a double payment the contact-year is Corporate where a live corporate subscription exists, otherwise Individual (Q-002).

A contact is in a live corporate subscription for a Campaign Year when they exist in Subs.vwCorpSubscriptions for that Sub Campaign Year and both 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' are active. 'Round' is not used, because a round is a tranche of processing corporate records and later rounds may change it (Mike, 2026-10-23), except as the third tie-break for a repeated key (RULE-128). The active value is taken to be 'Active' (Q-027), and the same value picks the copy of a repeated corporate subscription key that bronze lands (RULE-128).
Corporate firm-level discounts are not spread to individuals. The event carries the source's amount for the individual's own invoices, and the discount is a stated known gap (Q-005).
Payment method and payer type carry forward from the latest earlier invoiced year to years with no invoice. Concessions carry forward only when perpetual. Every carried value is flagged (Q-006).

Paid members by payment method, payer type and concession type are needed day by day. The daily count detail and the gold daily fact gain the three segment keys in their grain, and the annual rate base keeps its grain (Q-007, answered by Mike, AMD-007).
The concession reference is CE.vwConcessionType (Q-008).
Employer findings use the top 25 employers by paid members in the last full Campaign Year, and count individually funded members with a contact-record employer separately (Q-010).
Campaign Years before 2022, which the invoice source does not hold, get Not applicable (-2) for payment method, payer type and concession. They raise no invoice anomalies (Q-011).

When a contact-year has more than one eligible invoice, the latest by trans_date sets the contact-year's payment method, payer type and concession. When every invoice in a contact-year is fully credited, those invoices stand in as eligible for the segments and the invoice checks (Q-012).

Invoices are raised only when a member joins, renews or readmits, so each Join, Renewal or Readmission event has exactly one invoice. A contact with two such events in one Campaign Year has two legitimate invoices (Mike, 2026-10-23). For the invoice checks, events and invoices are paired in date order, and where invoices outnumber events the latest invoices are used (Q-022).
There is no Mixed payment method (Q-015).
The standard rate for the concession cross-check is the gross subscription line on the same invoice before the concession (Q-017).
Retired concessions are the six retired item codes used by Subs.usp_Refresh_SubsInvoices, and the comparison covers paid positions (Q-018).
corporate_account_ref holds the live corporate subscription's Scheme No (Q-019).
A free readmission is a Readmission whose event date falls in the second quarter of its Campaign Year, 1 January to 31 March for a Campaign Year starting 1 October (Q-023).
Removing silv_payment_events.payment_source breaks nothing downstream (Q-024).
Acceptance in this release is on synthetic data only, with no pass threshold for real data (for example minimum payment method coverage) (Q-026).

The Layercake column names used in this spec (for example silv_membership_events.event_date, contact_no, campaign_year and event_type; silv_data_anomaly columns; the Phase 1 paid position) are taken from the v1 draft and the Phase 1 baseline (Q-028).
A Join whose contact has no paid position in any year takes its segments and its amount, and is matched to an invoice, in the Join's own Campaign Year (Q-029).
subs_amount_gbp and invoiced_subtotal_gbp hold the same value on every event, because the view supplies a single invoiced amount (Q-044, answered by Product Owner assumption ASM-001).

The time an adjustment is written and the time T of an 'as known at' query use the database server's local time (SYSDATETIME(), as Layercake.etl_run_log does). Only adjustments written strictly after T are subtracted, so a change written exactly at T is part of the figure at T (Q-049).
An 'as known at T' query returns its first-load figures for a date first loaded after T, following the formula 'today's stored figure minus the changes written after T' literally (Q-050).

The adjustments review view has one row per cell, run and measure with a non-zero change, keeping the cell's grain columns and the time written, so changes that cancel out across cells stay visible (Q-051).

In Layercake.silv_member_state_ranges, valid_to is exclusive: a range covers [valid_from, valid_to), and a NULL valid_to is open-ended. A range is non-zero-length when valid_to is NULL or later than valid_from. Two non-zero-length ranges of one contact overlap when each starts before the other ends. Ranges that meet do not overlap, and a zero-length range never overlaps (Q-055, answered by Product Owner assumption ASM-012).

The repository holds no Power BI model or extract definition, so it cannot be shown that nothing outside the database reads fact_daily_member_count_detail.id. The design widens it to bigint and keeps it (Q-056, answered by Product Owner assumption ASM-012).

The AMD-006 speed target (daily count under 5 minutes, whole daily run under 15 minutes on a normal day) is the one real-data check in this release. A human checks it on production from Layercake.etl_run_log as a listed handover step. The agents' tests check on synthetic data that a normal run recomputes only the changed contacts and gives the same results as a full recompute, with no time limit. Q-026 still holds for data results (Q-057, answered by Product Owner assumption ASM-013).

Only a change to reference data covering dates from 2020-10-01 to the run date makes the daily count recompute the whole spine. The routine extension of ref_date_spine with dates after the run date, and the addition of a Campaign Year to ref_campaign_year_config that starts after the run date, do not (Q-058).

Every measure counted for a contact on a day, including the Join, Renewal, Readmission and Lapse counts, sits in the cell of the contact's attributes for that day's Campaign Year, so a contact stays in one cell per day. A Join whose first paid position is in a later Campaign Year is therefore counted in the daily fact under the attributes of the Join day's Campaign Year, while fact_membership_events carries the later year's (RULE-017). Daily Join counts by segment therefore need not match the event fact (Q-060).

A member with no local group (CE.vwContact.rics_localgroupid NULL, or a group CE.vwLocalGroup does not hold) gets local_group_id 0 Unknown and keeps their own country and their own country's region in every field, exactly as today (Q-062, answered by Q-066; Mike, AMD-009).

A member whose local group is inactive (statecode not 0), has no country, or whose row gives no region in either region field (apuk_worldregionid_name or Market_reporting_region NULL or blank) is treated as having no usable local group: local_group_id 0 Unknown, and their own country and their own country's region in every field. Fields are never mixed between the local group and the own country (Q-063, answered by Q-066; Mike, AMD-009).

CE holds only a member's current local group, with no history. The current local group applies to every date of the member's history, including closed Campaign Years, and a change of local group moves the whole history on the next run, as a change of country does (Q-064, accepted by Mike on 2026-11-26 and confirmed in AMD-009).
