open_questions.question: What is the grain of synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS: one row per invoice line with an item code, or one row per transaction (one total per invoice, as the Platform Schema describes synapse_fo.custtrans)? Please run the count-only profile in REQ-014 (RULE-095) and bring back the counts. Core query: WITH inv AS (SELECT ACCOUNTNUM, INVOICE, COUNT(*) AS row_cnt, COUNT(DISTINCT productcode) AS item_codes, MAX(CASE WHEN PostingType_Description LIKE '%tax%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_tax_row, CASE WHEN SUM(AMOUNTCUR) = MAX(CustTrans_AmountCur) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS lines_sum_to_total FROM synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS WHERE TRANSTYPE NOT IN (8, 24) AND INVOICE NOT LIKE '%CRE%' AND INVOICE NOT LIKE '%FTCN%' GROUP BY ACCOUNTNUM, INVOICE) SELECT row_cnt, item_codes, has_tax_row, lines_sum_to_total, COUNT(*) AS invoices FROM inv GROUP BY row_cnt, item_codes, has_tax_row, lines_sum_to_total ORDER BY invoices DESC; plus SELECT RICINVOICETYPE, PostingType_Description, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM synapse_fo.CUSTTRANS_RICS GROUP BY RICINVOICETYPE, PostingType_Description; plus SELECT rows_per_invoice, COUNT(*) AS invoices FROM (SELECT Account_Num, Invoice, COUNT(*) AS rows_per_invoice FROM Subs.tblSubsInvoices GROUP BY Account_Num, Invoice) x GROUP BY rows_per_invoice. Rules that depend on line grain: RULE-028 to RULE-030 (line-type mapping), RULE-014 (c) (fee-only invoices), RULE-044 (readmission fee check), RULE-049 (concession from the invoice's concession line) and RULE-077 (line landing scope). Event amounts no longer depend on it (REQ-008; Q-038). If CUSTTRANS_RICS is transaction grain, those rules cannot be applied from this source. Line types would then need a different source, such as synapse_fo.CUSTINVOICETRANS (invoice lines), which is in the external catalogue. Concessions might instead come from CE.vwConcession (per contact, with apuk_subscriptionyear). That means a new bronze landing and a design change before REQ-007, REQ-009 and REQ-011 are built. (Mike, human profiling step; review 1.1)
open_questions.answer: Answered from real data on 2026-11-11, counts only (Mike, AMD-002). CUSTTRANS_RICS is not one row per transaction. RECID is the customer transaction's key (it equals CUSTTRANSRECID), and each transaction is split into one row per ledger distribution: one row per POSTINGTYPE and ACCOUNTDISPLAYVALUE, the ledger account string that carries main account, cost centre, country, item code (productcode) and, where set, Campaign Year (RICSCAMPAIGNYEAR). 458,563 RECIDs occur on more than one row (1,015,865 rows): 456,807 invoice transactions (TRANSTYPE 2) and 1,756 payment transactions (TRANSTYPE 8). (RECID, POSTINGTYPE, ACCOUNTDISPLAYVALUE) is unique; (RECID, POSTINGTYPE, MainAccount, productcode) is not. brnz_subs_invoice_line lands every row in scope (RULE-077 unchanged), not aggregated, keyed on (recid, postingtype, accountdisplayvalue), and also lands postingtype, accountdisplayvalue, mainaccount, costcenter and ricscampaignyear (RULE-104). How the key is enforced is the Architect's call. AMOUNTCUR and AMOUNTMST are the line's own amounts. SETTLEAMOUNTCUR, and CustTrans_AmountCur and CustTrans_AmountMst if used, repeat on every line of a transaction and are taken once per RECID, including in the payment method's settled sums (RULE-013). Transactions and invoices are counted as distinct RECIDs (RULE-105). The rules that depended on this question keep CUSTTRANS_RICS as their source, read at this grain.

open_questions.answer: The earliest Campaign Year that has both a retired concession and a payment or settlement date. The date is the view's 'Renewal Date': the contact-year's first payment, or for a Full Concession invoice the settlement date, kept inside the Campaign Year (Mike, 2026-11-06).

open_questions.answer: Active, paid and event counts by date, region and grade stay unchanged, and both Phase 1 difference scripts still PASS. Only results split by membership status (Practising / Retired) change with the derived retirement date (Mike, 2026-11-06).

open_questions.question: Q-039's order is Readmission, then Renewal, then Join, then the earliest event date. When that leaves two or more events of the same type on the same earliest date in one contact-year, which event carries the amount?
open_questions.answer: The event with the lowest event_id carries the amount. The others carry null amounts and amount_status 'Counted on another event' (Mike, 2026-11-09).

open_questions.question: 'As known at' time T: the figure is today's stored figure minus the changes written after T. Which clock do 'written at' and T use: the database server's local time (SYSDATETIME(), as etl_run_log and the bronze audit columns use) or UTC? Is a change written exactly at T part of the figure at T, so that only changes written strictly after T are subtracted? Working default: server local time, and only changes written after T are subtracted.
open_questions.answer: Server local time (SYSDATETIME(), as Layercake.etl_run_log does). A change written exactly at T is part of the figure at T, so only changes written strictly after T are subtracted (Mike, 2026-11-17).

open_questions.question: 'As known at' time T for a date that had not been loaded yet at T: a first load writes no adjustment, so 'today's figure minus changes written after T' gives that date its first-load figure, as if it had been known at T. Should the view or function return those figures, or no figures for dates first loaded after T? Working default: follow the formula literally and return the first-load figures.
open_questions.answer: For a date first loaded after T, return its first-load figures, following 'today's stored figure minus the changes written after T' literally. No first-load time is tracked to hide them (Mike, 2026-11-17).

open_questions.question: Should the adjustments review view keep the cell's grain columns, with one row per cell, run and measure whose change is not zero? Or should it sum to one row per date, run and measure? Summing hides changes that cancel out, such as a corrected retirement date moving a member from Practising (-1) to Retired (+1). Working default: one row per cell, run and measure with a non-zero change.
open_questions.answer: Keep the cell's grain columns, with one row per cell, run and measure whose change is not zero. It does not sum to date level, so changes that cancel out across cells stay visible (Mike, 2026-11-17).

open_questions.question: RULE-128 tie-breaks when no copy of a repeated corporate subscription key has 'Sub Status' and 'Sub User Status' both active: does a copy with a NULL 'Sub User Created Date' lose to every copy with a date, or win? Is 'Round' (nvarchar(100)) compared as a number, so a later round beats an earlier one, or as text, and where does a NULL Round rank?
open_questions.answer: A copy with a NULL 'Sub User Created Date' loses to every copy that has a date. 'Round' holds text such as 'Round 1' and 'Round 2' in production, so it is not compared as text and not cast whole. It is compared by the whole number at its end (the digits after the last space, so 'Round 10' beats 'Round 9'). A NULL Round, or one that does not end in a whole number, counts as lowest. Any tie left after that is broken deterministically, so the same source data always lands the same row (Mike, 2026-11-18).

open_questions.question: For the overlap check (RULE-145): is valid_to in Layercake.silv_member_state_ranges exclusive, so that a range with valid_from = valid_to is zero-length and two ranges that meet do not overlap?
open_questions.answer: Yes, exclusive (Product Owner, ASM-012). usp_load_silv_daily_count counts a day in a range when [date] >= valid_from and [date] < ISNULL(valid_to, today + 1), the half-open interval [valid_from, valid_to). A range is non-zero-length when valid_to is NULL or after valid_from; two such ranges overlap when each starts before the other ends; a NULL valid_to is open-ended. Ranges that meet, and zero-length ranges, do not overlap.

open_questions.question: Does anything outside the database (for example the Power BI model or an extract) read fact_daily_member_count_detail.id, so that removing it would be unsafe?
open_questions.answer: Unknown from the repository, which holds no Power BI model or extract definition; nothing inside it reads id (Product Owner, ASM-012). Only reference rows from 2020-10-01 up to the latest date marked in etl_daily_count_loaded count (campaign_year_start on or before it for ref_campaign_year_config; silv_ref_membership_status in full); later spine dates and future Campaign Years are not a change.

open_questions.question: A contact-day takes the attributes of the Campaign Year of the day, and a contact sits in one cell per day. The event tables put a Join under the attributes of the contact's first paid position's Campaign Year (RULE-017). So a Join on 2024-06-01 (CY2024) whose first paid position is in CY2025 is counted in the daily fact (JoinEvents and ActiveMembers that day) under the CY2024 attributes, while fact_membership_events shows it under the CY2025 attributes. open_questions.answer: Yes. Every measure on a day uses that day's Campaign Year, so the one-cell rule holds; daily Join counts by segment need not match fact_membership_events.

open_questions.question: Once region follows the member's local group, which region flavour does the existing region field carry: the Finance mapping (South Asia in APAC), as the business Subs figures use, or the CRM world region, as Member Demographics uses? (AMD-008)
open_questions.answer: The existing region fields carry the region of the member's local group, so the figures match the local-group-based figures, on every date, including anything rebuilt or restated. The region is the local group's own region as CE.vwLocalGroup gives it for that local group row. Each existing field keeps the flavour it carries today: the world region field from apuk_worldregionid_name, and market_reporting_region from Market_reporting_region, both from the local group row. The region from the member's own country is kept in a new column, alongside the member's own country (contact_country_id), wherever that country is kept (Q-065) (Mike, 2026-11-26).

open_questions.question: What does a member with no local group get: one with no rics_localgroupid on CE.vwContact, or one whose group CE.vwLocalGroup does not hold? (AMD-008)
open_questions.answer: Answered by Q-066 (Mike, 2026-11-26; AMD-009). local_group_id 0 Unknown, and the member keeps their own country and their own country's region in every field, exactly as today.

open_questions.question: What does a member get whose local group has no country, or no region, in CE.vwLocalGroup? Is an inactive local group still used? (AMD-008)
open_questions.answer: Answered by Q-066 (Mike, 2026-11-26; AMD-009). A local group is usable only when CE.vwLocalGroup holds it, it is active (statecode 0), it has a country, and its row gives a region in both apuk_worldregionid_name and Market_reporting_region (not null or blank). An inactive group, a group with no country, or a group missing either region value is not usable. Its members keep their own country and their own country's region in every field, with local_group_id 0 Unknown, and fields are never mixed.

open_questions.question: Which local group applies to past dates and closed Campaign Years, given that CE holds only a member's current local group? (AMD-008)
open_questions.answer: Mike accepted the working default (2026-11-26), confirmed in AMD-009. The current local group applies to every date of the member's history, including closed Campaign Years. When a member's local group changes, their whole history moves on the next run, as a change of country does today.

open_questions.question: Where are the member's own country (contact_country_id) and the region from it kept, and do they join the grain? (AMD-008)
open_questions.answer: Mike accepted the working default (2026-11-26), confirmed in AMD-009. They are kept as new columns on every table that keeps country_id for a member (silv_member_base, silv_member_profile, silv_membership_events, fact_membership_events, silv_annual_rate_base, fact_annual_rate_base, silv_daily_count_detail, fact_daily_member_count_detail, etl_daily_count_cell_contacts and the daily count adjustment history). With local_group_id, they join the grain wherever country_id is in the grain.

open_questions.question: Mike's spec sign-off accepted the Analyst's working defaults for Q-062 to Q-065 'as written', but the draft that held them is not available to this version, which restates them in Q-062 to Q-065 and the assumptions. Do the restated defaults match what was accepted? If any differs, which wording applies?
open_questions.answer: No. The restated defaults differ from what Mike accepted (Mike, 2026-11-26, agreed in AMD-009). A member's local group gives their country and region only when it is usable: the member has a local group, CE.vwLocalGroup holds it, it is active, it has a country, and its row gives a region in both region fields. A member whose local group is missing, unknown, inactive, has no country or gives no region keeps their own country and their own country's region in every field, with local_group_id 0 Unknown. No field-by-field mixing. Q-064 (current local group for all dates) and Q-065 (wider table list) are accepted as written. RULE-170 to RULE-173 and AC-027-04 are amended to match.

open_questions.question: On deployment, every stored daily count date is restated so that members move from their own country's region and country to their local group's. Should those moves be written to the adjustment history like any other change (RULE-115), so the size of the move by region can be read from it? Pre-deployment rows keep their figures, and take contact_country_id equal to their country_id, the own-country region equal to their region, and local_group_id 0 Unknown. open_questions.answer: No adjustment rows for the deployment restatement (a change of basis, like AMD-007 RULE-162). Adjustment rows written before deployment keep their figures, take contact_country_id = their stored country_id and own-country region = their stored region, and local_group_id -2 Not applicable, because the local group was not recorded then (Mike, 2026-11-26, agreed in AMD-009). silv_ref_local_group and dim_local_group hold -2 Not applicable as a reserved row beside 0 Unknown, and no member is ever given -2. RULE-179 and AC-027-13 are amended to -2.
